subject: Diomede Islands
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about the Diomede Islands. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The island points are approximate: the islands are far smaller than a map pixel at this zoom, so they are marked, not outlined.

claims.text: The Diomede Islands are two rocky islands in the middle of the Bering Strait: Big Diomede, a Russian island, and Little Diomede, a U.S. island part of Alaska.
At their closest points the two islands are approximately 3.8 km (2.4 miles) apart.
The islands are separated by an international border which also defines the International Date Line in that area.
Big Diomede is 21 hours ahead of Little Diomede (20 in summer), according to locally defined time zones.
The islands are sometimes called Tomorrow Island (Big Diomede) and Yesterday Island (Little Diomede).
An ice bridge usually spans the distance between the two islands in winter.
Big Diomede Island is the easternmost point of Russia.
